issue.title: rest-cap (and quotaRest) set on a subscription provider is silently ignored: withPicks doesn't carry RestCap/QuotaRest
issue.body:
## Summary

`magpie provider rest-cap <id> 6h` writes `restCap: 360` into `providers.json`, but for subscription (signed-in account) providers the value never reaches the runtime provider — routing keeps using the default cap (10 minutes, 30 when rate limited). Key-based providers work fine.

## Repro

1. On a subscription provider (e.g. `antigravity`, `workbuddy-ai`, `commandcode-plan` — any provider that comes from `Accounts()` rather than a user-typed key):

   ```
   magpie provider rest-cap antigravity 6h
   magpie provider rest-cap antigravity
   # Antigravity · a key or account that keeps failing sits out at most 10 minutes, 30 when rate limited (magpie's own)
   ```

2. `providers.json` does contain `"restCap": 360` on the `antigravity` record, so the write succeeded — but the read-back still shows the default.

3. Same command on a key-based provider (`cloudwise`, `xiaomi`, `opencode-go`) updates and reads back correctly (`sits out at most 6 hours`).

## Root cause

`internal/provider/provider.go` — `allProviders()` builds account-backed providers from `Accounts()` and merges the user's `providers.json` record via `withPicks(a, pk)`. The field list in `withPicks` copies `Models`, `Routing`, `Affinity`, `AccountCaps`, `MaxConcurrency`, `MaxRPM`, … but **not `RestCap`** (and `QuotaRest` is missing too). So for any provider whose provider object is an account clone, the user's rest cap (and quota rest) is dropped and the gateway's `RestCapOr(longestRateRest)` falls back to the default.

Suggested fix: add `a.RestCap, a.QuotaRest = pk.RestCap, pk.QuotaRest` to `withPicks` (they are safe, per-provider knobs like the rest of the copied set).

## Impact

The per-provider rest cap is one of the main levers against fallback chains re-probing a repeatedly failing member every request (TTFT cost). On subscription providers — often the primary member of a routing group — the knob silently does nothing, so repeated 429/unknown failures only back off to 10/30 minutes.

Verified on magpie 0.1.1278 (macOS arm64).

comments.body: This is the same defect as #3076, where a patch is already waiting: `withPicks` (internal/provider/provider.go:675) copies the provider's picks onto each signed-in account but leaves out `QuotaRest`, `QuotaResetAt` and `RestCap`, so the cap never reaches subscription accounts — the same one-line omission covers `quota-rest` too. Branch with the commit: [hunt53-d-restcap](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt53-d-restcap) (head `048abe41`), patch and verification on [#3076](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3076#issuecomment-6293991542).

修了，在分支 [skygunner:fix/account-rest-cap](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/account-rest-cap)（commit c41b6fe，基于 main 87d703c5）。README 说本仓库不开 PR，放在这里供取用。

按你的建议把 `withPicks` 补上了，一处修两个入口（All 的主账号 + logins_on 的 AlsoOn 账号）：

- 补的三个字段：`RestCap`、`QuotaRest`，以及同一族的 `QuotaResetAt`（#2008 的 `quota-rest until` 时刻——Save 路径在账号记录上同样保留它，合并时也被丢，和 restCap 一模一样的漏法，属同一类 sibling）。
- 其余字段对照过 Save 在账号记录上保留的字段清单（provider.go:816 那行），没有别的遗漏：Hidden/Quiet/Tucked 走各自的 hiddenAccount/quietAccount 路径，不算。

**验证**（`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8`、`umask 022`；commit body 有完整记录）

- 新增 `TestAccountKeepsItsRests`（googleSandbox 的 antigravity 双账号 fixture）：改动前红——合并后的账号 cap 0 / quota 0 / at ""——改动后绿，Find 的主账号与 AlsoOn 的每个账号都带上三值（队列设置的 #1899 同款断言）。
- `TestQuotaRestUntil`、`TestRestCapCmd` 与 internal/provider 包其余测试不变全绿；三平台 vet/build 通过；全量 `go test -tags nogui ./...` 67 ok，除 main 既有两红（#2207、#3280）外无新增（`TestOpenCodeSessionOnEveryCall` 今天有一次全量负载红，单跑/包内/其余两次全量绿，已单独立案 #3284）。

verified — I checked out `skygunner:fix/account-rest-cap` (`c41b6fe`, based on `main` `87d703c5`, an ancestor of today's tip `95be6bb7`) and re-ran the checks on it.

Coverage vs. our [#3076](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3076) branch (`hunt53-d-restcap`, `048abe41`): the two commits carry the same one-line fix — the same three fields (`RestCap`, `QuotaRest`, `QuotaResetAt`) copied at the same spot in `withPicks` — so they cover the same ground: the accounts `All` builds and every account `AlsoOn` returns; neither has a field or an entry the other lacks. The tests differ: theirs asserts a two-account antigravity fixture end to end (`Save` → `Find` → every `AlsoOn`), ours asserts `withPicks` directly plus a `SetRestCap` write/read round trip with the `off` case. No new commit from me; our #3076 branch stays as a fallback, and either commit heals #3076 the same way.

Verification (`GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, go1.26.8, darwin/arm64; `-tags nogui` where noted):

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Ablation, red | fix reverted (`git checkout c41b6fe~1 -- internal/provider/provider.go`, new test kept), `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run TestAccountKeepsItsRests ./internal/provider/` | FAIL — `account_rests_test.go:42: the account's rests: cap 0, quota 0, at ""` (exit 1) |
| Ablation, restored | `git checkout c41b6fe -- internal/provider/provider.go`, same command | `ok ... 0.993s` (exit 0) |
| Existing tests | `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run 'TestQuotaRestUntil\|TestRestCapCmd' -v ./internal/cli/` (they live in `internal/cli`) | both PASS |
| Package full | `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/provider/` | `ok ... 73.547s`, no failures |
| Race, targeted | `go test -tags nogui -race -count=1 -run TestAccountKeepsItsRests ./internal/provider/` | `ok ... 2.027s` |
| gofmt | `gofmt -l` on the two changed files | empty |
| vet, darwin | `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/provider` | clean |
| vet, linux | `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./internal/provider` | clean |
| vet, windows | `GOOS=windows go vet -tags nogui ./internal/provider` | clean |
| build, darwin | `go build -tags nogui ./internal/provider` | ok |
| build, linux | `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui ./internal/provider` | ok |
| build, windows | `GOOS=windows go build -tags nogui ./internal/provider` | ok |
| Applies to tip | provider.go blob identical between `87d703c5` and `95be6bb7`; `git merge-tree --write-tree 95be6bb7 c41b6fe` | no conflict; the fix line lands in `withPicks` |

Red without the fix (the fix reverted, the new test kept):

```
--- FAIL: TestAccountKeepsItsRests (0.10s)
    account_rests_test.go:42: the account's rests: cap 0, quota 0, at ""
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider	1.043s
```

Green again once `provider.go` is restored.

Verified with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode); I've read the diff and re-ran the checks above.

issue.title: provider: rest-cap is ignored for subscription accounts (withPicks doesn't copy RestCap), so 529 overload benches most of a Codex pool

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

`magpie provider rest-cap <id> …` (added for #2008 in v0.1.1230, `off` in v0.1.1236) is **silently ignored for subscription-account providers such as `codex`**. The value is written to `providers.json`, but it never reaches the provider the gateway routes with, so every Codex account keeps the built-in 1 → 2 → 4 … 10 min ladder after a 529.

Under sustained upstream overload this benches most of a Codex account pool. A related gap: a plain (non-group) provider has no limit on tries or total time per request, so a caller with its own fallback has to wait for every account to be asked.

## Cause

`internal/provider/provider.go` `withPicks(a, pk)` copies the provider's settings from `providers.json` onto each signed-in account: `AccountConcurrency`, `QueueLimit`, `QueueWait`, `MaxRPM` and others. It **does not copy `RestCap`**. `restAfterMarked` then reads `c.p.RestCap` / `c.p.NoFailRest()` from that merged provider, so the cap is always 0 (magpie's own).

Checked on the `v0.1.1236` tag and on `main` at `75e769a9f` (2026-10-20); `withPicks` is the same in both. Reading the code, `QuotaRest` / `QuotaResetAt` seem to be missing from `withPicks` too. I have not verified those two at runtime.

## Repro (v0.1.1236, `--network none`, fake Codex sign-in)

1. Start `ghcr.io/yetone/magpie:0.1.1236` with a fake `home/.codex/auth.json` (an unsigned JWT is enough for magpie to list one Codex account) and `providers.json` = `{"providers":[{"id":"codex","name":"","key":"","sink":true,"maxConcurrency":5}]}`.
2. Run `magpie provider rest-cap codex 1m`.
3. `providers.json` now has `"restCap": 1` (`off` writes `-1`), but:
   - the CLI's own echo right after the write still says `a key or account that keeps failing sits out at most 10 minutes, 30 when rate limited (magpie's own)`, and
   - `GET /api/providers` on the running server shows no `restCap` for `codex`.

Expected: the cap applies to the provider's accounts, the same way `account-concurrency`, `queue-limit` and `rpm` do.

## Impact we measured (0.1.1226 in production, one day of `routing/*.jsonl`, about 9.1k requests / 15.8k tries, Codex only)

- In peak hours about 62% of tries end in `529 server_is_overloaded`. This is vendor-side: the rate is similar across accounts, plans and egress paths.
- Each 529 on a non-last candidate rests that account. At peak, a median of 15–18 of 20 accounts were resting, so each request rotated among about 6 accounts. Conversation affinity broke for 60% of requests (15% off-peak), and the cache-read ratio on the moved requests fell from 0.94 to 0.81, with P10 at 0.12.
- After a 529, the next try succeeds about 28% of the time on another account and about 22% on the same account after the 1s/2s pause. So switching accounts is right. The multi-minute rest is what hurts, because a vendor-wide overload is not the account's fault.
- Requests that finally failed with 529 took a median of 6 tries and 23.5s (P90 60s, P99 119s). By then the 15s keep-alive has already sent the 200 headers to the caller.

## Asks

1. **Bug:** copy `RestCap` (and probably `QuotaRest` / `QuotaResetAt`) in `withPicks`, so `rest-cap` works for subscription accounts.
2. **Feature (optional):** a per-provider cap on tries or total time per request for plain providers, e.g. `magpie provider max-tries <id> <n>` or a total-time budget. Then a caller with its own fallback (a gateway in front of magpie) can take over sooner, instead of waiting for every account to be asked.
3. **Discussion (optional):** treat `529 server_is_overloaded` like `codexReset` (move to the next account without resting it), or give it a much shorter rest than other unknown failures.

Happy to test a build against the same routing data.

issue.title: Feature request: global default rest cap in Settings and Docker configuration, with provider overrides

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Request

Please expose a **global default rest cap in Settings**, shared by providers and their model candidates unless a provider has an explicit override, and persist the same setting in the normal configuration file for Docker/headless deployments.

Today, changing the default across a deployment means setting `magpie provider rest-cap <id> ...` separately for each provider. Newly added providers do not inherit an administrator-chosen default, and the GUI has no editor for this option.

## Current behavior checked

- Running the official Docker image `0.1.1472`; a read-only `magpie provider rest-cap nvidia` reports the built-in limits: 10 minutes for repeated failures, 30 minutes when rate limited.
- Latest main inspected: `a3232e3e1199eff783af905c37681eb15ae7dc89`.
- [Provider.RestCapOr](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/a3232e3e1199eff783af905c37681eb15ae7dc89/internal/provider/concurrency.go#L342) reads the provider's `restCap` or uses the caller's built-in default. I could not find an equivalent global field in `internal/settings`.
- The provider editor preserves a CLI-set value when saving, but does not expose an input for it.

## Desired behavior

1. Add a clearly labeled global default in Settings, with a duration and a way to restore Magpie's built-in defaults.
2. Use the precedence **explicit provider override → global default → existing built-in defaults**. Providers without an override, including newly added providers, should inherit it without copying a value into every provider record.
3. Apply the resolved default wherever the existing rest-cap mechanism already applies, including existing model-scoped rests. “Global” means a shared default value, not a shared failure counter or a rest affecting every provider/model.
4. Document and persist the same setting for Docker/headless installations, so an administrator can configure it through the mounted configuration directory without using the GUI. Please document the field name, units and reload/restart requirements.
5. Show the effective value and whether it is inherited or overridden. Preserve existing provider overrides and existing behavior when no global value is configured.

For example, setting a global cap of 30 minutes should cover providers A and B with no override, while provider C explicitly set to 5 minutes keeps 5 minutes. Adding provider D should automatically inherit 30 minutes.

The UI/documentation should distinguish the default failure cap (currently 10 minutes) from the rate-limit cap (currently 30 minutes). If an explicit duration follows the existing per-provider `RestCap` behavior and applies to both, please say so. If an “off” option is exposed, it should retain its existing limited meaning: no rest after an unknown failure, not disabling quota/credit/authentication handling.

## Scope

This is a configuration and discoverability request. It does not request changing which errors cause cooldown, expanding 400/422 classification, introducing multi-day automatic freezes, or making soft cooldown a hard circuit breaker.

Related: #2008 (configurable rest parameters), #3076 and #3176 (provider override propagation). This request focuses on the remaining global-default and Settings/Docker configuration surface.
